title: Conductor Relay Sentry for toolchain feedback and loop liveness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Design and implement a lightweight 'Conductor Relay Sentry' layer in the execution path that mediates multi-tool chaining, enforces structured output contracts during streaming, and provides robust recursion/loop liveness guards. Goal is to close gaps observed in production where chained tools cause replay loops, malformed injected results, and streaming clients receive inconsistent partial JSON blobs. The sentry will be a thin policy layer between orchestrator and tool adapters: it validates tool-return envelopes, synthesizes streaming placeholders for in-flight tool calls, enforces token budgets, and signals deterministic fallbacks when loop heuristics fire.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor correctly accepts/rejects tool result envelopes against JSON schema for 100% of test fixtures
Streaming sessions with in-flight tool calls produce well-formed structured frames (start/tool-call/result/end) observed by SDKs
Recursion detector triggers protective fallback within 200ms of detecting a loop pattern and prevents >95% repeat call storms in load tests
Compatibility shim allows legacy tool adapters without structured-response support to run with a best-effort wrapper and a logged migration warning
Telemetry events instrumented for every sentry decision: validation_failure, recursion_probability_high, budget_exhausted, compatibility_wrapped
design_notes: Placement: Sentry sits in the executor post-invoker, pre-merge step. It must be stateless per-request and rely only on request-local transient state plus a short-lived in-memory store for recursion fingerprints

Envelope contract: tool results must be wrapped as {"tool": "<id>", "status": "ok|err|partial", "payload": <structured>|null, "meta": {"exec_time_ms": 0}}. Sentry will coerce legacy plaintext payloads into {"text": <str>} when compatibility shim triggers

Streaming framing: use four frame types: FRAME_START, FRAME_TOOL_CALL, FRAME_TOOL_RESULT, FRAME_END. SDKs will ignore FRAME_TOOL_CALL/RESULT unless they advertise tool-aware streaming. This prevents partial JSON mixing into free-form streams

Recursion detection: combine three signals — call-stack depth (strict counter), token-budget remaining (soft cutoff), and semantic repetition score using cached embeddings similarity of last 3 tool payloads (threshold 0.88). Use a scoring function that biases for depth first, then semantic similarity to reduce false positives

Fallback policy: on high recursion probability, automatically short-circuit to configured fallback model variant (lower-capacity read-only path), respond with a structured error explaining degraded behavior, and open a debug trace for offline analysis

Compatibility layer: provide an adapter wrapper (CompatAdapter) that can wrap legacy tool implementations and produce the envelope contract. It should be opt-in per-tool and emit migration telemetry. Default config for new deployments turns on wrapper globally in permissive mode for 72h rollout window

Observability: expose per-request headers for sentry decisions (X-Sentry-Id, X-Sentry-Decision, X-Recursion-Score) to allow tracing in Console; surface aggregate dashboards for validation failures and wrapper usage
decisions: Enforce envelope contract at the boundary; do not allow internal callers to bypass the sentry
Adopt embedding-based semantic loop detector instead of naive string equality to catch paraphrase loops
Use a soft token-budget alarm (percent remaining) to inform recursion score rather than immediate hard cutoff to avoid disrupting legitimate deep pipelines
Expose tool-aware streaming frames to SDKs rather than embedding tool results inline in raw text streams
CompatAdapter will log & metric migration surface, but will not permanently coerce payload shapes — teams must opt in to migrate tool code
tradeoffs: Latency: extra validation and embedding similarity check adds ~6-12ms median overhead; justified by high reduction in loop incidents and malformed output complaints
Complexity: added sentry layer increases surface area for bugs; mitigated with staged rollout, feature flags, and e2e contract tests
Compatibility: wrapper masks legacy bugs temporarily, which could delay proper tool fixes; resolved by telemetry-driven migration deadlines
Memory: maintaining short-lived fingerprints for recursion detection consumes ephemeral memory proportional to concurrent in-flight toolchains; bounded by LRU with 1000-entry cap
implementation_tasks: Define envelope JSON schema and publish to docs + SDKs
Implement Conductor Relay Sentry module in runtime: validation, framing, compat wrapper, recursion scoring
Integrate lightweight embedding service call for semantic similarity (use cached internal embed table to avoid external deps)
Add feature flag (sentry.v1.enabled) with per-team override and rollout schedule
Update JS/Go SDK streaming decoder to recognize frame types and honor tool-aware streams
Add unit + integration tests including adversarial loop simulations and legacy-tool compat tests
Create Console dashboard panels for sentry metrics and an alert rule for validation failure spikes
Prepare migration doc and deprecation plan for tools relying on inline plaintext results
testing_plan: Unit tests: envelope validation edge-cases, malformed inputs, compat wrapper coercions
Simulations: synthetic RL workloads that chain 8-12 tools under varying latencies to verify recursion detector and fallback triggers
Load tests: 10k RPS with mixed tool chains; verify overhead and memory bounds
Consumer integration: update SDK test harness to parse and verify stream frames across versions
Canary: enable sentry.v1 for 5% of hosted API traffic with verbose logging for first 48h
